rows.description: An adult brings food, shows up, listens and offers practical help to a bereaved family. Presence and small tasks are worth more than perfect words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A toddler settles more easily with the same song, story or sequence each night. Predictable shared routines make the family feel like a safe place.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child joins in prayers, festival lights or birthday traditions and delights in doing them right. Doing what the family does makes them feel like one of us.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: Children invent secret handshakes, club names and rules. The made-up ritual matters because it marks who belongs and who does not.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager wonders why a ritual is done and whether they believe in it. They feel a tension between love for the family and wanting to own their beliefs, and respectful questions are part of growing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: affection, admiration, curiosity, awe

rows.description: A teenager learns to belong to a community while holding some private views. Belonging does not need total sameness, and healthy groups allow some difference.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A new student is asked to do humiliating tasks to join a group. The wish to belong is powerful, and shared hardship can bond people but should never involve harm or coercion.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Missing home rituals abroad or in a hostel [Receiver]
rows.description: A young person away from home misses the small daily rituals like family meals and festival mornings. They feel a quiet homesickness and often create small new rituals to feel anchored.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtype: Creating new rituals in a new life [Actor]
rows.description: A newly married or newly employed adult builds their own traditions such as a weekly dinner or a team coffee. Shared rituals turn a group of individuals into a community.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtype: Attending a ritual without full belief [Observer]
rows.description: An adult attends a family ritual they do not fully share and sees what it means to the elders. They can take part with respect and honesty without pretending or contempt.
